texts: An early diastolic murmur, a wide pulse pressure of 148/45 mmHg and heart failure point to chronic aortic regurgitation.
The left ventricle dilates enormously, so the chest film shows cor bovinum, a huge heart: A is the answer.
The apical diastolic rumble is the Austin Flint murmur, not the Gallavardin phenomenon, which belongs to aortic stenosis.
A carotid shudder belongs to aortic stenosis, and a pulsatile liver to tricuspid regurgitation.
